title: Finite-support polynomial presentation in a separable tensor square
statement:
Let $k\subseteq L$ be a separable algebraic extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Put $R=L\otimes_k L$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with the commutative algebra structure and maps $\iota(c)=c\otimes1$ and $\mu(a\otimes b)=ab$ of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. For every $x\in R$ there exist $n\geq0$, $a_i,b_i\in L$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, a subfield $E=k(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\subseteq L$ finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] and separable over $k$, an element $\alpha\in E$ with $E=k(\alpha)$, and polynomials $g_i\in k[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], such that
$$x=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\otimes b_i,\qquad b_i=g_i(\alpha).$$
Let $P\in k[T]$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$, let $\overline P,\overline g_i\in L[T]$ denote the polynomials obtained by including their coefficients into $L$, and put $t=1\otimes\alpha$ and $F=\sum_i a_i\overline g_i\in L[T]$. For $G=\sum_j c_jT^j\in L[T]$ write $G(t)=\sum_j\iota(c_j)t^j\in R$. Then $P$ and $\overline P$ are separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], and
$$\overline P(\alpha)=0,\qquad \overline P(t)=0,\qquad F(t)=x,\qquad F(\alpha)=\mu(x).$$
The assertion includes $x=0$ and the choice of an empty sum, for which $E=k$ and $\alpha=0$ are allowed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], pure tensors generate $R$ as a $k$-module, so write $x=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\otimes b_i$: any $k$-scalar in a linear combination can be absorbed into $a_i$ by bilinearity. Set $E=k(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\subseteq L$. Each $b_i$ is algebraic over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] makes $E/k$ finite-dimensional. Every element of $E$ is an element of $L$ with the same polynomial evaluation over $k$, hence is algebraic and separable over $k$ by that same definition. This verifies the separability hypothesis for $E/k$ without requiring $L/k$ to be finite.

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, finite-subextension paragraph; Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, generation in its construction; Fields Tag 09GH, lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-primitive-element] to the finite separable extension $E/k$ to choose $\alpha\in E$ with $E=k(\alpha)$. Since $\alpha\in L$ is algebraic over $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis] gives a basis $1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{d-1}$ of $E$, where $d=[E:k]$. For each $i$ write $b_i=\sum_{j<d} c_{ij}\alpha^j$ with $c_{ij}\in k$, and define $g_i(T)=\sum_{j<d}c_{ij}T^j$. These are the required polynomial representatives, with $b_i=g_i(\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 030N, lemma-primitive-element, moreover clause; Tag 09GN, lemma-degree-minimal-polynomial, with Tag 09G7, example-degree-simple-algebraic-extension

proof.text: Let $P$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$. Its defining properties in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] give $P(\alpha)=0$ and separability of $P$. By [def-pc-separable-polynomial], choose $U,V\in k[T]$ with $UP+VP'=1$. Put bars on coefficients using $k\hookrightarrow L$. Coefficientwise addition and convolution multiplication in [def-weil-polynomial-ring] give $\overline U\,\overline P+\overline V\,\overline{P'}=1$, and the explicit derivative formula gives $\overline{P'}=(\overline P)'$: the coefficient $j c_j$ maps to $j\overline{c_j}$. Thus the same Bezout identity witnesses separability of $\overline P$ by [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Also $\overline P(\alpha)=P(\alpha)=0$ in $L$.

source.place: Tag 09H1, definition-separable; coefficientwise expansion of its coprimality identity, as used in Algebra Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal

proof.text:
Put $t=1\otimes\alpha$. The multiplication and the two $k$-algebra maps of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give $t^j=1\otimes\alpha^j$ for every $j\geq0$ (including $t^0=1\otimes1$). For $g=\sum_j c_jT^j\in k[T]$, bilinearity and the balancing relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore give
$$\overline g(t)=\sum_j(c_j\otimes1)(1\otimes\alpha^j)=\sum_j c_j\otimes\alpha^j=1\otimes\sum_j c_j\alpha^j=1\otimes g(\alpha).$$
Here $c_j$ in the first tensor factor denotes its image in $L$; balancing applies because $c_j\in k$. Taking $g=P$ proves $\overline P(t)=1\otimes0=0$, and taking $g=g_i$ gives $\overline g_i(t)=1\otimes b_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C2X, lemma-separable-algebraic-diagonal, polynomial-to-tensor calculation; Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, bilinearity relations

proof.text:
Set $F=\sum_i a_i\overline g_i\in L[T]$. Distribute the finite coefficient sums in the stated definition of evaluation. Step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give
$$F(t)=\sum_i\iota(a_i)\overline g_i(t)=\sum_i(a_i\otimes1)(1\otimes b_i)=x,$$
and direct evaluation in $L$ gives $F(\alpha)=\sum_i a_i b_i=\mu(x)$. The last equality follows by applying the multiplication homomorphism from that cited node to the expansion of $x$. For $x=0$ choose $n=0$, $E=k$ and $\alpha=0$ instead: $k$ has basis $1$ over itself, each of its elements has linear minimal polynomial $T-c$, and $P=T$ for $\alpha=0$ by the least-degree characterization in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Hence $E/k$ is finite separable, $E=k(0)$, $P'=1$ witnesses separability by [def-pc-separable-polynomial], and $F=0$, $t=0$ give all four asserted identities.
